title: Readings in Taoism
description: Selected readings from important Taoist texts. Depending on the year, primary sources will be read in original Chinese or in translation.

title: (Chinese) Aesthetics and Critical Theory
description: What does it mean to aestheticize politics? Is politics inherently aesthetic? Is there such a thing as “apolitical aesthetic”? Why and how to study aesthetic theory comparatively? What is the relationship between aesthetics, modernity, and critical theory? This course explores the major issues and frameworks of critical theory by probing into the question of aesthetics; it also treats modern Chinese culture as an aesthetic and political project, focusing on theories of (Chinese) modernity, media, literature, film, and the relation of aesthetics and politics.

title: World Literature and Modern China
description: This course investigates the histories and theories of World Literature as a world-making ideology and as a discipline in comparative literary studies. It focuses on modern Chinese literature and culture while joining current debates on globalization and cosmopolitanism

title: China in the World
description: Investigates the histories and theories of World Literature as a world-making ideology and as a discipline in literary studies. Particularly, it participates in current debates on globalization and cosmopolitanism by focusing on the case of modern Chinese literature and culture.

title: Readings in Chinese Buddhism
description: Selected readings in important Buddhist texts which were either originally written in Chinese or translated into that language. Depending on the year, primary sources will be read in original Chinese or in translation.

title: Queer China, Crip China
description: Study of the representation of non-normative bodyminds and desires (e.g. disability and homosexuality) in modern Chinese literature and film. We discuss the meanings embedded in Chinese discourses of gender, sexuality, and disability; investigate how these discourses have been appropriated in the construction of a modern Chinese national identity; and connect our specific inquiry into Queer China and Crip China to our general attempt to answer the broader question of how the modern nation-state China has been imagined into being over the past century. Our approach will be interdisciplinary, comparative, and transnational.

title: Graduate Research Seminar on Modern China
description: Research seminar in the history of modern China. Students conduct historical research in a seminar contact using both primary and secondary source materials, to produce an original and substantial research paper. Graduate students will receive extra readings from their instructor and will complete a longer research paper at the end of the course.

title: Special Topics
description: Seminar in special areas of interest in Chinese cultural studies. Specific course titles and topics to be announced by the department each quarter offered. Course content will vary.

title: China in the World
description: This course investigates the histories and theories of World Literature as a world-making ideology and as a discipline in literary studies. Particularly, it participates in current debates on globalization and cosmopolitanism by focusing on the case of modern Chinese literature and culture.

title: Development of East Asian Countries
description: A focus on economic development in East Asian countries, topics include causes of development; relationship between poverty, inequality, and economic development; education and economic development; population aging; industrialization and urbanization; global warming, pollution control and sustainability.

title: Queer China, Crip China
description: Studies the representation of non-normative bodyminds and desires (e.g. disability and homosexuality) in modern Chinese literature and film. Discusses the meanings embedded in Chinese discourses of gender, sexuality, and disability; investigates how these discourses have been appropriated in the construction of a modern Chinese national identity; and connects our specific inquiry into Queer China and Crip China to our general attempt to answer the broader question of how the modern nation-state China has been imagined into being over the past century. The approach is interdisciplinary, comparative, and transnational.

title: US-China Trade Relations
description: Offers an economic approach for addressing the US-CHINA trade related issues in an effort to prepare UCSB students for the complex realities of US-CHINA trade and economic diplomacy. Provides students with an understanding of international political economy and the major trade related issues and challenges facing the US-China relationship.

title: Apprentice Teaching
description: Apprentice teaching. This course consists of supervised teaching practice in Chinese language.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate standing and consent of instructor. Employment in this department teaching assistant or linguistic informant.

title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual tutorial. A written proposal for each tutorial must be approved by department chair and filed with graduate division.

title: Preparation for Comprehensive Examinations
description: Study for master's comprehensive examinations and Ph.D examinations.

title: Master's Thesis Research and Preparation
description: Instructor should be chair of the student's thesis committee.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

title: Ph.D. Dissertation Preparation
description: Terminal preparation of the dissertation.

title: Masterpieces in Chinese Literature
description: Examines a selection of works from Chinese literature, with the goal of understanding the major genres and their development over time. The cultural roles of literature, as well as criteria for critical evaluation, are also addressed.

title: The Ancient Greeks
description: An introduction to the literature and culture of ancient Greece. The study of literary and material remains will illustrate how the Greeks lived and the values they expressed through literature and the arts. Topics may include the rituals and festivals of Greek religion, the conflict between heroic ideals and democratic ideology, the institutions that shaped public and private life, and the competitive nature of law, drama, athletics and politics.

title: The Ancient Greeks - Honors
description: A discussion section led by the instructor, provided for students in the honors program. Students receive one unit for the honors seminar (20AH) in addition to four units for Classics 20A.
prerequisites_raw: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 20A and consent of instructor.

title: The Romans
description: An introduction to the civilization of the ancient Romans. Topics such as Romes legends of male and female virtue, Augustuss ingenious transformation of the republic into a monarchy, gladiators and chariot racing, slavery, Rome and the Christians, and the competing philosophical systems of Stoicism and Epicureanism will be explored through literary texts and archaeological remains. Encounter a range of sources from Livy, Virgil, and Seneca to monuments of the emperors, and examine the complex legacies of Roman culture across time.

title: The World of Heroes
description: A study of the Iliad, the Odyssey, the Aeneid and other ancient epics, and of the place of these works in Greek and Roman society. The course explores how the epic hero embodies a cultures ideals concerning the individual, the community, and the universe.

title: World of Heroes - Honors
description: A discussion section led by the instructor, provided for students in the honors program. Students receive one unit for the honors seminar (36H) in addition to four units for Classics 36.
prerequisites_raw: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 36; consent of instructor.

title: Gender and Sexuality in Greece and Rome
description: Study of gender and sexuality in a wide range of Greek and Latin texts and contexts, exploring diverse ideals of masculinity and femininity, and sexual codes, norms, and practices.

title: Gender and Sexuality in Greece and Rome-Honors
description: Discussion section led by the instructor, provided for students in the honors program. Students receive one unit for the honors seminar (39H) in addition to four units for Classics 39.
prerequisites_raw: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 39; consent of instructor.

title: Greek Mythology
description: Introduction to the principal myths of ancient Greece and the ways in which these myths have been understood. Format and readings vary.

title: Greek Mythology--Honors
description: A discussion section led by the professor is available to students in the honors program. Students will receive one unit for the honors seminar (40H) in addition to four units for Classics 40.
prerequisites_raw: Concurrent enrollment in Classics 40 and consent of instructor.

title: Introduction to Classical Archaeology
description: Examines the techniques and methods of classical archaeology as revealed through an examination of the major monuments and artifacts of the Greco-Roman world from prehistory to the Late Empire.
